This application is filed under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, BNSS), seeking pre- arrest bail.
2. The applicant is the accused in Crime No.31/2026 of Chalakudy Police Station, Thrissur District.
The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The prosecution case, in short, is that the applicant by making the de facto complainant to believe that the amount shall be repaid within one month, obtained 4 sovereigns of gold ornaments, 2 sovereigns of gold chain, one sovereign of bracelet, one sovereign of jimikky, a total of 64 grams of gold, on 15.07.2023 in front of Edassery Finance, Chalakkudy for pledging and obtained Rs.5 lakhs.
The amounts had been obtained without any intention to pay back and thereby committed the above offences.
4. I have heard Sri.Rebin Vincent Gralan, the learned counsel for the applicant and Sri.M.C.Ashi, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicant submitted 2026:KER:10129 BAIL APPL. NO. 481 OF 2026 that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicant with the alleged crime;
hence, he is entitled to bail.

The learned Senior Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, submitted that the alleged incident occurred as part of the applicant's intentional criminal acts, and if he is released on bail at this stage, it will affect the course of the investigation.
6.
The law regarding the grant or refusal of pre- arrest bail is well settled.
Pre-arrest bail cannot be granted as a matter of course.
The power under Section 482 of BNSS could be exercised only when a special case is made out, that too, recording reasons thereof.
Perusal of the case diary reveals that the accusation made against the applicant is very serious in nature, and it prima facie shows a premeditated criminal act on his part.
The crime was registered pursuant to a private complaint filed by the defacto complainant before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Chalakudy.

sentences.text: There is a clear recital in the private complaint that the applicant has executed an agreement on 24.07.2023, in which he has admitted the receipt of gold ornaments from the defacto complainant and agreed to return the same.
The said 2026:KER:10129 BAIL APPL.
NO. 481 OF 2026 agreement has been produced along with the private complaint.
7. The investigation is in a preliminary stage.
The custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary for the investigation.

As rightly argued by the learned Public Prosecutor, the possibility of the applicant influencing the witnesses and interfering with the investigation cannot be ruled out if Biju K. K vs State Of Kerala on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177251052/
2 he is released on bail.
